about.description: I move science data for a living. By day I'm a research networking systems engineer at ESnet, helping high-energy physics pipelines get their petabytes across the country; by night you'll find me in a data-frame, a P4 compiler, or a good baseball stat sheet.
details: My path ran through San Diego first: at the San Diego Supercomputer Center (UCSD) I led the SEAM project, worked on the National Research Platform's Kubernetes substrate and its FABRIC integration, taught the platform's intro courses, and spent a lot of late nights making P4 programs run on programmable FPGAs.

In 2026 I joined ESnet at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory as a research networking systems engineer, where the fun is data movement: software-defined networking for high-energy physics, SENSE orchestration, and interop between the tools scientists actually use to move files.

Off the clock I keep a long-lived list of side projects — a baseball WAR calculator in R, image-generation experiments, competitive-programming problem sets — and I unironically believe every big idea deserves a small weekend experiment.
